why: rclc ships a second registration entry point whose callback also receives the `rmw_request_id_t`. Ours has one registration verb: the correlation token is an `int64_t` sequence number that `rclc_polling_client_send_request_raw` returns and `rclc_polling_service_send_response_raw` takes back (see the service stage's `cpp:Client::create_request_header`), and it belongs to the ENTITY, not to a second `add_*` overload. A registration entry point per callback shape is the `executor-owns-no-entity-storage` rule seen from the executor's side.
